verdict.rationale: Logseq ships a documented local HTTP API server that gives authorized external access to the graph: a single POST /api endpoint dispatches any plugin-API method, including the logseq.Editor and logseq.DB namespaces, with bearer-token auth and worked curl examples. A coding agent can therefore read the graph and write to it (e.g. logseq.Editor.insertBlock) programmatically without driving the GUI. missing for 10: an official MCP server, a truly app-independent headless mode (the server must first be enabled in the desktop app's Features settings), first-party rather than community-driven method docs, an OpenAPI spec or versioning policy, and independent hands-on corroboration of agent use.
